purpose: Phase C semantic gates. Assertions that detect MEANING rather than hash movement, built in response to the B1 finding that five materially different corruptions produced one byte-identical failure line.

motivation.finding: The B1 mutation battery, run twice, showed that inverting CW/CCW semantics, inverting a paired score sign, admitting right-censored dwells to the uncensored likelihood, removing the motor-leakage guard, and falsifying the protocol freeze date ALL produce exactly one failure line: SHA-256 mismatch for experiments/results/observed-experiment-report.json.
motivation.diagnosis: The suite detected that a hash moved. It could not say what changed or why it mattered.
motivation.response: Four gates that assert the scientific property directly, none of which routes through any digest.

acceptanceCriteria: A1 FAIL on target corruption, PASS clean
A2 failure message NAMES the semantic property

corruptionDetection.failureNamesProperty: TRAIN/HOLDOUT MOTOR INDEPENDENCE IS NOT ENFORCED

launderingResistance.attack: declare the audit own TIMING_UNVERIFIED record PROSPECTIVE
delete the adverse provenance record entirely

comparisonWithPriorSignature.before: one identical SHA-256 mismatch line for all five corruptions
comparisonWithPriorSignature.after: four distinct messages, each naming the violated property

prospectivityGateSignificance: This gate fails when a prediction and its result appear in the same commit. It would have caught correction C5-1, in which this audit committed the exact provenance defect it found in the repository. It ships with a worked record documenting that failure and an assertion that fails if the record is deleted, so the adverse finding cannot be quietly erased.

gates.summary: This gate asserts train/holdout motor independence as a semantic property rather than as a byte identity. It has three parts: G1 constructs a synthetic dataset in which one motor ("MOTOR-IN-BOTH-PARTITIONS") contributes 4 uncensored events to each partition and asserts runObservedExperiment refuses it with a refusal that names leakage; G2 recomputes the preregistered split function sha256(motorName) mod 5 with node:crypto and checks every motor's stored partition against it, plus a hash-free disjointness check on the real frozen dataset; G3 proves no holdout observation reaches a fitted parameter, first against hand-calculated training-only values on a synthetic fixture (1.75 s vs a pooled 9.625 s; 12.5/31 vs a pooled 42.5/61), then on the real dataset by multiplying every holdout duration by 37 and forcing every holdout direction to "on" and asserting fittedOnTrainingOnly is bit-identical while heldoutResults moves. The hardest design decision was making the leaking synthetic fixture pass every downstream eligibility floor (>=20 train events, >=20 holdout events, >=5 distinct holdout motors) so that with the guard deleted the dataset analyses to completion and returns a finished report claiming audit.noMotorLeakage = true — the failure then reads as "the guard is gone" rather than as an unrelated eligibility error. The second hardest was pairing the real-data invariance assertion with a live negative control, since an invariance test passes vacuously if the perturbed field is being silently dropped.
gates.targetCorruption:

To verify the gate works, remove that line and run `node --test tests/semantic/train-holdout-leakage.semantic.test.mjs`. VERIFIED EXECUTED: G1 fails, G2 and G3 still pass, and the repository was restored byte-identical afterwards (`cmp` clean, `git status --porcelain` shows only the new tests/semantic/ directory).

Three further corruptions were applied and verified caught, each in isolation with restore-and-cmp afterwards:

(1) Message laundering: change the guard's message to "Invalid dataset configuration." while keeping the throw. G1 fails on the /leak/i match, with the message "The leaking dataset was rejected, but NOT for leakage...". This closes the obvious escape from a plain assert.throws.

(2) A motor spanning both partitions in the real frozen data (the second half of the stated target). Applied by moving motor 18-02-05-1710 from holdout to train in experiments/data/wadhwa-2022-events.json while leaving splitRemainder lying at 0. G2's recomputation test fails and prints the offender: `{"motorId":"18-02-05-1710","storedPartition":"train","storedRemainder":0,"recomputedRemainder":0,"requiredPartition":"holdout"}`. Note this corruption is invisible to the disjointness check alone (moving a motor wholly to one side keeps the sets disjoint) — it is caught only because the split is re-derived from the motor name rather than read from the file.

(3) Fit leakage: change stateMeans to `mean(uncensored.filter(e => e.stateN === stateN)...)` so holdout durations enter the normalisation. Both G3 tests fail — the synthetic one reports "Observed 9.625 s" against the hand-calculated 1.75 s, and the real-data one reports `fittedOnTrainingOnly.normalizedDurationModels.lognormal.mu changed from -1.242927074547147 to -2.8903121379561463`.

Clean-tree baseline: all 5 tests pass in ~1.5 s. `npx eslint` on the file is clean.
gates.failureMessageOnCorruption:
For the primary target (guard deleted), the literal message is:

  TRAIN/HOLDOUT MOTOR INDEPENDENCE IS NOT ENFORCED.
  runObservedExperiment ACCEPTED a dataset in which motor 'MOTOR-IN-BOTH-PARTITIONS' contributes 4 uncensored events to the training partition and 4 to the holdout partition, and returned a finished report claiming audit.noMotorLeakage = true over 6 holdout motors.
  The preregistered unit of independence is the motor/cell (experiments/preregistration.v1.json -> scope.unitOfIndependence, split.leakageControl, qualityGates: 'No motor may appear in both train and holdout partitions'). With that rule unenforced, every held-out claim (H1, H2, H4) is scored partly on motors whose own events set the fitted parameters, so the reported held-out advantage is no longer a held-out quantity.

The named semantic property is train/holdout motor independence at the declared unit of independence. The message also surfaces the specific lie the corrupted code tells — the returned report still asserts audit.noMotorLeakage = true — which is the truth-laundering signature, not a digest delta.
gates.independenceArgument:
A3 (no hash routing): the gate never computes a sha256 of a file, never reads runId, never touches experiments/results/*.json, public/*.json, or audit-manifest.json. Deleting every artifact digest in the repository would leave G1 and G3 completely unaffected — G1 depends only on runObservedExperiment's control flow over an in-memory fixture, and G3 depends only on the arithmetic relation between fitted parameters and their inputs. G2 does call node:crypto, and this needs a precise defence: it hashes a MOTOR NAME, not a file, and it does so because `sha256(motorName) mod 5` IS the preregistered split function (experiments/preregistration.v1.json -> split.method). Re-deriving a scientific definition is not the same operation as comparing an artifact digest: the sha256 here is a pseudorandom assignment rule whose scientific content is "the partition is a fixed function of identity, not of outcome", and the failure message says exactly that. Its verified failure output names a motor and the partition the rule requires — it does not report that bytes moved. G2's first test (disjointness) uses no hashing at all and would survive the deletion of node:crypto entirely.

A4 (not a circular oracle): nothing in this file compares a fresh computation against a stored artifact the same implementation wrote. The three oracle classes used are all external to the implementation. First, a control-flow oracle: does the function refuse this input, and does the refusal name the property — the answer is a throw or a return, not a number produced by the pipeline. Second, hand arithmetic: 52.5/30 = 1.75 and (12+0.5)/(30+1) = 12.5/31 were computed by a human from the fixture defined in this file, and the fixture is constructed here rather than read from disk; critically, the assertion is discriminative, because the pooled alternatives (9.625 and 42.5/61) are stated explicitly and are far away, so the test distinguishes "training-only" from "pooled" rather than merely pinning whatever the code emits. Third, an invariance/ablation oracle: the expectation is not a value but a relation — perturbing only holdout inputs must not move any fitted output. That relation is a statement about the function's dependency structure and can be checked without knowing any correct value, which is exactly why it survives arbitrary changes to the numbers. The paired negative control (heldoutResults MUST move) prevents the invariance from passing vacuously, which is the standard failure mode of invariance tests and the one that would otherwise make G3(b) a no-op.
limitations: G2's split re-derivation reads the holdout/training remainder classes FROM experiments/preregistration.v1.json. An attacker who edits both the preregistration (swapping which remainders are holdout) and the dataset consistently would pass G2. G2 constrains the split to be a fixed function of motor identity covering 0..4 exactly once; it does not pin WHICH remainder class is the holdout. Pinning that would require an independent record of the frozen protocol, which this gate deliberately does not fabricate.

The gate does not detect leakage at units coarser than the motor. If two motorIds are in fact the same physical cell, or the same culture/day appears on both sides, every assertion here passes. `18-02-05-1710`-style names suggest date-stamped recordings, so day-level clustering is plausible and unaddressed.

G3(b) proves that fitted parameters do not depend on holdout VALUES. It does not prove they are free of holdout influence through COUNTS or structure: eligibleStates is computed from holdout event and motor counts (lib/observed-experiment.js:305-307), so the set of states analysed genuinely is a function of the holdout partition's size. That is a real, small, preregistered dependency this gate does not flag.

The G1 fixture reaches the guard through the public surface only. No internal of lib/observed-experiment.js is exported for direct testing (the module exports mean, sampleVariance, fitDurationModels, posteriorSlowGivenSurvival, runObservedExperiment — the split logic, filtering, and the guard itself are not exported). The gate is therefore an end-to-end behavioural test of runObservedExperiment; it cannot localise WHICH internal step lost the guard, only that the composite function no longer refuses.

No coverage of the other four mutations in the battery: CW/CCW direction inversion, model-comparison sign inversion, right-censored admission into the uncensored likelihood, and protocol freeze-date falsification. Each needs its own semantic gate. In particular, G3(b) forces every holdout direction to 'on', which is adjacent to but does not test direction semantics.

The synthetic fixture uses a single primary state (N=1). Cross-state effects — a state-mean for one N contaminated by another N's events — are not exercised synthetically; they are covered only indirectly by G3(b) on the real dataset.

protocol.uncertainty.replicates is lowered to 24 in G3(b) for runtime. The claim that replicate count cannot affect a fitted parameter is verified by inspection of fitDurationModels (which never reads protocol) rather than asserted by the test itself.

gates.summary: This gate asserts the frozen protocol's two-part censoring rule as behavior, not as a digest: right-censored dwells must be excluded from the uncensored duration likelihood, and simultaneously retained in the observation record for provenance. It runs `runObservedExperiment` (the only public entry point; the cohort filter at lib/observed-experiment.js:295 is an internal local and is NOT exported, so the gate is built entirely on the public surface) against a synthetic 68-dwell fixture whose per-state means are exact integers by construction: 24 uncensored training dwells of 1/3/5 s sum to 72 s giving a mean of exactly 3 s, while the 24 right-censored 1 s dwells would drag the mean to exactly 96/48 = 2 s if admitted. Both values are exact binary floats, so no tolerance is needed and the oracle is arithmetic done by hand in a comment, not a number read back from the pipeline. The hardest design decision was proving the exclusion is actually happening rather than merely that a number is stable: a single assertion that the mean is 3 could pass vacuously if the fixture never contained a discriminating censored dwell. That is solved with three runs of the same implementation over three inputs — flags present, censored rows physically absent, and flags stripped — asserting that (a) the flagged run yields the excluded value 3, (b) the flag-stripped run yields the included value 2 and larger cohorts, proving the fixture discriminates, and (c) the flagged run is numerically identical to the censored-absent run, which is the general invariant that a correctly excluded observation exerts zero influence on any likelihood quantity. Retention is asserted separately: after the run the censored dwells are still in the record, still flagged, still direction-null, and the provenance census minus the two likelihood cohorts equals exactly the censored count.
gates.targetCorruption: Mutation M06: delete `!event.rightCensored && ` from lib/observed-experiment.js:295, so the line reads `const uncensored = dataset.events.filter((event) => states.includes(event.stateN));`. This admits right-censored dwells into the uncensored duration likelihood. To verify the gate works, apply exactly that deletion (e.g. `perl -pi -e 's/\!event\.rightCensored && //' lib/observed-experiment.js` on an isolated copy) and run `node --test tests/semantic/censoring-exclusion.semantic.test.mjs`. VERIFIED IN AN ISOLATED COPY (the repository working tree was never mutated): clean tree = 6 pass / 0 fail, reproduced twice identically; under M06 = 2 pass / 4 fail. The two surviving tests are by design — "the fixture discriminates" already strips the censoring flags so it is invariant to the mutation, and the protocol-text check does not read code.
gates.failureMessageOnCorruption: CENSORING SEMANTICS VIOLATED: the training mean dwell time for state 2 is 2 s, but excluding the right-censored dwells gives exactly 3 s by hand (72 s over 24 uncensored dwells). A value of 2 s means right-censored dwells ENTERED the uncensored duration likelihood, contradicting the frozen protocol rule 'exclude it from uncensored duration likelihoods'.  [Three further named failures fire alongside it: "CENSORING SEMANTICS VIOLATED: removing the right-censored dwells from the record changed the fitted/held-out result ... (field: fittedOnTrainingOnly.stateMeanDurationS)"; "CENSORING COHORT ACCOUNTING VIOLATED: 48 events entered the training likelihood but only 24 uncensored eligible training dwells exist in the record. The surplus is 24 right-censored dwell(s) that must have been excluded."; and "CENSORING BOOKKEEPING VIOLATED: the gap between the retained provenance census and the combined likelihood cohorts must be exactly the number of right-censored dwells (34). It is 0."]
gates.independenceArgument: A3 — no hash path. The file contains no import of node:crypto, no sha256, no runId read, and no comparison against experiments/results/observed-experiment-report.json, public/, or dist/. It computes the report object in memory and asserts named semantic fields (fittedOnTrainingOnly.stateMeanDurationS, cohort.trainEvents, cohort.holdoutEvents, cohort.sourceEvents, heldoutResults.*). runId is never read, and the report objects are never compared wholesale. If every hash in the repository were deleted the gate would behave identically. The one file it reads is experiments/preregistration.v1.json, and it reads the human-readable rule TEXT (asserting it still says retain / provenance / exclude / likelihood), not any digest of it.  A4 — not a circular oracle. The expected values 3, 2, 24, 48, 25 and 35 are arithmetic performed by hand in the header comment over a fixture defined in the test file itself: 8x1 + 8x3 + 8x5 = 72 over 24 dwells = 3; (72+24)/48 = 2. They were not read back from any pipeline output or stored artifact — a reader can check them with a pencil. The cohort counts asserted against the report are recomputed inside the test by its own independent filter over the fixture array (`event.partition === p && event.stateN === STATE && event.rightCensored === false`), not taken from the implementation. The one cross-run comparison (Run A vs Run B) is not artifact comparison: both sides are freshly computed in this process from two inputs that differ only by the presence of rows the protocol says must not matter, so it asserts an invariance property of the implementation, not agreement with something the implementation previously wrote. Nothing on disk is trusted as an oracle.  A5 — determinism. Pure function calls, a fixed protocol seed (20260717) and replicate count (8), no Date/Math.random/network, no dependence on experiments/upstream-cache/. Confirmed by two consecutive identical clean runs.  A2 — every assertion carries a message naming the semantic property (CENSORING SEMANTICS / CENSORING COHORT ACCOUNTING / PROVENANCE RETENTION / CENSORING BOOKKEEPING / FROZEN PROTOCOL RULE), including the observed and hand-calculated values, so the reader learns "censored dwells entered the likelihood".
limitations: Does NOT test the ingestion stage. scripts/ingest-wadhwa-data.py is what decides WHICH dwell is the last one and sets rightCensored; a corruption that mislabels or fails to flag the final dwell upstream would leave this gate green, because the gate supplies its own already-flagged fixture.

The internal `uncensored` filter at lib/observed-experiment.js:295 is a function-local constant and is NOT exported. The gate therefore observes censoring treatment only through what runObservedExperiment surfaces in its report (state means, cohort counts, held-out scores). A censoring error confined to a quantity the report does not expose would be invisible.

cohort.sourceEvents is copied from dataset.ingestion.eventCount, which this test supplies. The provenance-census assertion therefore proves the report faithfully reports the full census alongside the reduced likelihood cohorts; it does not independently verify that the real dataset's ingestion.eventCount counts censored dwells.

The retention half is a non-mutation check (censored rows still present, still flagged, still direction-null, duration intact after the run). It catches exclusion implemented by deletion or by relabelling, but a pipeline that simply never touches the input array passes it trivially.

Runs on a single state (N=2) with a deliberately coarse three-valued duration fixture. Distribution-fitting pathologies, multi-state eligibility interactions, and the mixture/Weibull/lognormal fits themselves are not being validated here — only which events enter them.

Verified against exactly one mutation (M06 as specified). It is not claimed to detect the other four corruptions in the battery (direction inversion, score-sign flip, leakage-guard removal, protocol freeze-date falsification); those need their own semantic gates.
Assertions on the frozen protocol text are keyword-level (retain / provenance / exclude / likelihood). A rewrite that preserves those four words while inverting the rule's meaning would pass.

gates.summary: This gate asserts that "on" means outcome 1 in the direction predictor, and that every quantity named a "mixture advantage" is oriented (mixture - baseline). It drives the public runObservedExperiment over a synthetic two-state fixture in which direction is determined by stator state with certainty (state 1 always "on", state 2 always "off") and durations are drawn by deterministic inverse-CDF from the M3_UNI_TWO_TIMESCALE mixture itself, making M0/M1/M2 mis-specified by construction. The hardest design decision was making the direction constants exactly hand-calculable: choosing 60 train and 40 holdout events per state makes the Jeffreys pooled estimate exactly 60.5/121 = 0.5, so globalLogLoss is exactly ln 2 and globalBrier exactly 0.25, while stateConditionedLogLoss is exactly -ln(60.5/61). That symmetry is deliberate — the pooled baseline is INVARIANT under the M01 outcome flip, which isolates the state-conditioned number as a clean orientation probe rather than a value that moves for two reasons at once. The second decision was to catch M05 three independent ways: a by-construction sign assertion, an algebraic identity against meanLogScoreNatsPerEvent (aggregated by a different expression in the implementation), and a full recomputation of the paired advantage from log-density formulas written from their textbook definitions inside the test file. Verified: 11/11 pass clean; M01 fails 2 tests, M05 fails 4 tests, and a double inversion (train side plus holdout side, which cancels in the log losses) still fails 2 tests via the training-probability and onFraction assertions. npx eslint is clean.
gates.targetCorruption:
Two corruptions, both verified by mutating an isolated scratchpad copy of lib/observed-experiment.js (the user's working tree was not modified).

M01 — direction outcome inversion, lib/observed-experiment.js:276 inside directionMetrics():
  apply: `const outcome = event.direction === "on" ? 1 : 0;`
      -> `const outcome = event.direction === "on" ? 0 : 1;`
  observed result: 2 of 11 tests fail ("direction semantics: held-out outcome 1 is on ..." and "anchoring identity: state-conditioned direction predictor was constructed to beat the pooled baseline"). stateConditionedLogLoss moves from 0.00823049913651548 to 4.8040210447332505; logLossImprovement moves from +0.6849 to -4.1109.

M05 — paired score sign inversion, lib/observed-experiment.js:327 inside runObservedExperiment():
  apply: `mixtureVsWeibull: mean(scored.map((event) => event.logScores.mixture - event.logScores.weibull)),`
      -> `mixtureVsWeibull: mean(scored.map((event) => event.logScores.weibull - event.logScores.mixture)),`
  observed result: 4 of 11 tests fail (by-construction sign, bootstrap-interval sign, independent recomputation, and the mean-log-score linearity identity). mixtureVsWeibull moves from +0.10209798980543132 to -0.10209798980543132 — exact negation.

Adversarial variant also verified — a "repaired" double inversion that flips BOTH the training-side counts (lines 228/315/319, `=== "on"` -> `=== "off"`) AND the holdout outcome at line 276. The log losses cancel and remain numerically correct, but 2 tests still fail: onProbabilityByState[1] reads 0.0082 instead of 60.5/61, and stateSummary onFraction reads 0 for the all-"on" state.

Clean tree: 11/11 pass in ~390 ms. `npx eslint tests/semantic/orientation-direction-and-score-sign.test.mjs` exits 0.

NOT YET WIRED: package.json `test` script enumerates test files explicitly and does not include tests/semantic/. The gate must be added to that list (or the script switched to a directory glob) or it will never run in CI. I did not edit package.json — that is a user-owned config change outside the scope I was given.

and, from the same run:

    In this fixture state N determines direction with certainty, while the pooled predictor is exactly a coin flip. The state-conditioned predictor MUST win.

and:

Every message names the semantic property (on/off outcome polarity; which model was constructed to beat which) and states the direction of the error. None reads "hash mismatch" or "deepStrictEqual failed".
gates.independenceArgument:
A3 — not a hash check. The file imports exactly two things: node:test / node:assert/strict, and runObservedExperiment from lib/observed-experiment.js. There is no node:crypto import, no sha256, no reference to runId, no read of experiments/results/observed-experiment-report.json, experiments/data/, experiments/preregistration.v1.json, or experiments/upstream-cache/. There is no node:fs import at all. Deleting every digest in the repository and every committed artifact would leave all 11 tests passing unchanged. The gate reads nothing from disk; the dataset and the protocol object are both constructed in memory in this file.

A4 — not a circular oracle. Nothing is compared against a stored artifact this implementation wrote. Four independent oracle layers:

(1) Closed-form arithmetic. The direction constants are derived by hand from integer event counts through the Jeffreys rule (k+0.5)/(n+1) and written as the literal expressions -ln(60.5/61), ln 2, (0.5/61)^2, and 0.25. These come from the fixture's construction, not from any run. The counts are chosen so 60.5/121 = 0.5 exactly, making globalLogLoss exactly ln 2 with no floating-point slack.

(2) By-construction ordering. The holdout durations are drawn by deterministic inverse-CDF from the M3_UNI_TWO_TIMESCALE family itself (w=0.7, rf=5, rs=0.3/0.86, chosen to satisfy the mean-one constraint the implementation enforces). M0/M1/M2 are mis-specified by construction, so the sign of every paired advantage is known a priori. The direction fixture makes state N determine direction with certainty while the pooled predictor is exactly a coin flip, so state-conditioning must win a priori. Neither sign is read from the pipeline.

(3) An independently written scoring oracle. independentLogDensity implements the exponential, Weibull, lognormal, and two-exponential-mixture log densities from their textbook definitions in this file, and the paired advantages are recomputed from scratch over normalized holdout durations whose state means are also recomputed here from the training events. It shares no code with lib/observed-experiment.js. Only the FITTED PARAMETERS (shape, scale, sigma, mu, weightFast, rateFast, rateSlow) come from the report — these are parameters, not scores, and the corruption under test lives in the scoring orientation, not the fit. The Jacobian -log(scale) is identical across a pair and cancels exactly, which is why it can be omitted. Agreement on the clean tree is ~4e-16; under M05 the disagreement is an exact negation.

(4) An internal cross-aggregate identity. mean(a_i - b_i) = mean(a_i) - mean(b_i) is exact. meanLogScoreNatsPerEvent and pairedMixtureAdvantageNatsPerEvent are produced by two different expressions in the implementation (lines 472 and 325-329), so transposing one and not the other breaks the identity by exactly 2x.

A vacuity guard is included: the first test asserts the fixture actually cleared the eligibility rule and that all 80 holdout events were scored, so the later assertions cannot pass by operating on an empty set.
limitations: Covers only 2 of the 5 undetected mutations. It does nothing about the right-censoring admission, the removed motor-leakage guard, or the falsified protocol freeze date. Those need their own gates.

Not wired into CI. package.json's `test` script enumerates test files explicitly and does not include tests/semantic/; until that list is extended (or converted to a directory glob) this gate never runs. I did not edit package.json.

The independent recomputation in section 5 takes the FITTED PARAMETERS from the report. A corruption inside fitDurationModels that produced wrong-but-self-consistent parameters would be invisible here — the oracle would score the same wrong model both ways and agree. Parameter recovery is a separate gate's job.

Only the exported surface is exercised. directionMetrics, scoreEvents and logDensity are not exported, so per-event rows and the per-event logScores object are never inspected directly; the gate reads only aggregates off the returned report. A corruption that cancels within an aggregate but is wrong per event would survive.

A total relabeling at the data layer — where the ingestion script itself writes "on" where the trace shows "off" — is not detected, because this gate builds its own labels. It pins the code's interpretation of the label, not the label's fidelity to the recorded trace.

The paired-advantage sign assertions rely on the fit converging sensibly on the fixture. Verified margins on the clean tree are +0.4225 (vs exponential), +0.1021 (vs Weibull) and +0.0393 (vs lognormal) nats/event. The lognormal margin is the thinnest; a future change to the optimizer's bounds or grid could in principle move it toward zero and make that one assertion flaky. The Weibull comparison — the one M05 actually targets — has a 10x wider margin.

The bootstrap-interval assertions depend on the implementation's seededRandom. They are degenerate on this fixture (every motor carries events in both states, so every replicate is balanced and lower === upper for the direction interval). A change to the resampling scheme could alter them without any orientation error being present.
Asserts nothing about the real 1349-event dataset, by design. It proves the code's orientation is correct on constructed data; it does not verify any number in the released report.

The M05 mutation as specified touches only the point estimate at line 327. The parallel bootstrap expression at line 344 is asserted only through the interval-contains-point-estimate check; a mutation applied to line 344 alone would be caught by that check but with a weaker message.

Tolerances are 1e-11 (hand-calculated values) and 1e-9 (recomputation and linearity identity). These are far tighter than any corruption of interest (the smallest signal here is a 0.039 nats/event sign flip) but are not derived from a formal error analysis of the optimizer.

gates.summary: This gate asserts that a prediction is prospective only if the git commit that first introduced the prediction file is a STRICT ANCESTOR of the commit that first introduced each result artifact it governs. It defines a prediction record format carrying claim, falsifier, madeAgainstCommit anchor, predictionPath, resultPaths, and a DECLARED prospectivity class; the gate independently MEASURES that class from the commit DAG and fails when declaration and measurement disagree. The hardest design decision was reconciling requirement 3 (fail loudly on same-commit) with A1 (pass on the clean tree): the repository's own B1 re-run prediction and its ledger really were committed together in b675978, so a gate that simply failed on same-commit would be permanently red and would be deleted. The resolution is that the gate asserts HONESTY OF DECLARATION rather than absence of the defect — a record honestly declaring TIMING_UNVERIFIED passes, and the loud failure fires the instant anyone upgrades it to PROSPECTIVE. That makes this class of dishonesty structurally impossible while keeping the adverse provenance result permanently visible instead of buried. Ordering is decided purely by `git merge-base --is-ancestor`; author and committer timestamps are never consulted, because they are attacker-supplied strings (GIT_COMMITTER_DATE) while ancestry cannot be forged without rewriting every descendant commit id including HEAD.
gates.targetCorruption:
TARGET: prospectivity laundering — declaring a prediction PROSPECTIVE when the commit graph cannot witness that it preceded its result. This is the M11 defect (a preregistration claiming to predate results it actually postdates) relocated to an oracle the author cannot forge by editing a field.

HOW TO APPLY IT (verified, exit-0 on clean tree, exit-1 corrupted):

  cd <repo> && perl -0pi -e 's/prospectivity: "TIMING_UNVERIFIED",/prospectivity: "PROSPECTIVE",/' tests/semantic/prospectivity-provenance.test.mjs
  node --test tests/semantic/prospectivity-provenance.test.mjs

This upgrades the B1-RERUN-ON-C3-FIXED-TREE record — whose prediction file (audits/phase-b/b1-rerun-prediction-committed-before-execution.txt) and result ledger (audits/phase-b/b1-mutation-ledger-rerun.json) both entered history in commit b675978 — from an honest TIMING_UNVERIFIED to a false PROSPECTIVE claim.

OBSERVED on the clean tree: 11 pass, 0 fail, 0 skipped. Ledger printed:
  B1-MUTATION-BATTERY-V1: declared=PROSPECTIVE measured=PROSPECTIVE (STRICT_ANCESTRY_PROVEN)
  B1-RERUN-ON-C3-FIXED-TREE: declared=TIMING_UNVERIFIED measured=TIMING_UNVERIFIED (SAME_COMMIT:...)

OBSERVED corrupted: 2 independent tests fail — "Declared prospectivity equals prospectivity measured from commit ancestry" and "The known same-commit provenance defect remains declared and visible".

A second, structurally different corruption also fires: replace madeAgainstCommit with any 40-hex string naming no object (e.g. "deadbeef" x5) and the "Every prediction anchor commit exists and precedes the prediction it anchors" test fails with FABRICATED PROSPECTIVITY ANCHOR. Setting the anchor to a commit that is a DESCENDANT of the prediction (e.g. b675978 on the B1-MUTATION-BATTERY-V1 record) fires PROSPECTIVITY ANCHOR INVERTED — the direct commit-graph analogue of M11's forward-dated freeze.

Also verified: eslint clean; and running the file from a directory that is not a git work tree produces "PROSPECTIVITY GATE: NOT_RUN — not inside a git work tree" with 9 tests SKIPPED (not passed).

(and, from the second failing test)

The B1 re-run record has been upgraded to 'PROSPECTIVE'. Its prediction and its ledger were committed together in b675978; no ordering was ever witnessed. Upgrading it launders an unverified timing claim into a prospective one.

The named semantic property is PROSPECTIVITY: whether a prediction entered history strictly before the result it governs. The message states the declared class, the measured class, the reason code, and the two commit ids that decide it. Nothing in the message mentions a hash, a digest, or a byte.
gates.independenceArgument:
A3 — NOT A HASH CHECK. The file contains no sha256, no crypto import, no runId, no artifact digest, and no read of experiments/results/*. Its only two input sources are the prediction records and the `git` binary, invoked through exactly five plumbing commands: `rev-parse`, `cat-file -e`, `log --diff-filter=A --format=%H`, `merge-base --is-ancestor`, and (in fixtures only) `init`/`add`/`commit`. Delete every hash in the repository — every pin in audit-manifest.json, every embedded source digest in run-observed-experiments.mjs — and this gate behaves identically. Conversely, recompute every hash in the repository so all digest gates go green, and this gate still fails on a laundered prospectivity claim, because a digest cannot express an ORDER between two commits.

A4 — NOT A CIRCULAR ORACLE. The gate never compares a fresh computation against an artifact the same implementation wrote. The measured value comes from the git commit DAG. That DAG is written by git, from human commit actions, before this gate existed; the analysis pipeline (run-observed-experiments.mjs, run-science-gates.py, the walkthrough generator) cannot write it and cannot alter it. The declared value comes from a human-authored record. The two are produced by disjoint processes and the gate asserts they agree. Crucially, the DAG is TAMPER-EVIDENT in a way a stored artifact is not: to make a same-commit pair look prospective you must rewrite history, which changes the id of the rewritten commit and every descendant including HEAD — a change visible to every collaborator and every other clone, and not achievable by editing any file in the working tree. This is the property a stored report can never have, because the report and the value it stores are written by the same act.

The synthetic fixtures satisfy A6 with hand-calculable expectations: seven temporary repositories are built with commit orders written literally in the test body (prediction-then-result; both-together; result-then-prediction; prediction-only; prediction-plus-uncommitted-result; a pair whose child commit bears an EARLIER timestamp than its parent; a bogus 40-hex object id). The expected class for each is derivable by reading the fixture, with no reference to the 1349-event dataset, no reference to any pipeline output, and no tolerance to justify. The timestamp fixture is a deliberate negative control: it would pass under a timestamp-based classifier only by accident and would break a naive one, proving the classifier reads topology rather than clocks.

A5 — determinism. No network. No wall-clock read: the gate never calls Date.now(), never parses a committer date, and the one fixture that sets GIT_COMMITTER_DATE does so to fixed literal strings in order to prove timestamps are IGNORED. No dependence on experiments/upstream-cache/ — that path does not appear in the file. Fixtures are created under os.tmpdir() and removed on process exit.
limitations: It proves ORDER, not HONESTY OF CONTENT. A prediction can be committed in an ancestor commit and still be vague, unfalsifiable, or written after peeking at a result that existed only in the author's working tree and was committed later. Git witnesses when a file entered shared history, not when a thought occurred. The schema test enforces a substantive claim and falsifier field, but cannot judge whether the falsifier is a real risk.

A single author with push access to a branch nobody else has fetched can construct any ancestry they like before publishing, by committing the prediction first and the result second even though both were authored together. The guarantee only becomes strong once the prediction commit has been pushed to a remote or observed by a second party. The gate cannot detect this; it verifies structure, not witness. Adding signed tags or an external timestamping service would close it, and neither is in scope here.

It does not verify that the prediction record's resultPaths list is COMPLETE. A record can name one result artifact prospectively while a second, adverse artifact produced by the same run goes unlisted and therefore unordered. Nothing here enumerates which artifacts a given prediction ought to govern.

It does not cover experiments/preregistration.v1.json itself. The M11 mutation edited a frozenAt STRING inside that file; this gate would catch the same class of dishonesty only if a prediction record were written naming the preregistration as its predictionPath and the observed-experiment report as its result. That record is not included, because on the current history the preregistration and its results are not separated by a commit boundary — writing one would have made the gate red on the clean tree. The machinery is ready for it; the history is not.

Renames are invisible to it. `git log --diff-filter=A` without --follow treats a renamed prediction file as introduced at the rename commit. That is conservative for predictions (it makes PROSPECTIVE harder to claim) but ANTI-conservative for results: renaming a result artifact moves its measured introduction later and could make a same-commit pair look prospective. A rename of a result path is therefore an undetected evasion.

Merge commits are excluded via --no-merges. A prediction or result introduced solely by a merge resolution would measure as not-in-history and classify TIMING_UNVERIFIED. That is conservative but will produce confusing NOT_RUN and TIMING_UNVERIFIED reports on merge-heavy workflows.

It reports NOT_RUN, not FAIL, on shallow clones and non-git trees. CI that runs with fetch-depth 1 will silently skip every ordering check. The NOT_RUN line is printed to stderr and the tests show as SKIPPED rather than PASSED, but a summary reader counting only failures would miss it. Release validation must run this gate on a full clone.

The worked records are embedded in the test file rather than stored as experiments/predictions/*.prediction.json. The disk scanner exists and is exercised, but the two canonical records live in the same file as the gate, so a single edit removes both the record and its checker. Test 5e partially defends this by asserting the B1 re-run record is still present and still declared TIMING_UNVERIFIED, but nothing prevents deleting the whole file.

whatThisDoesNotFix: The hash chain remains. These gates ADD semantic detection; they do not remove the regression lock.
The five corruptions are now detected semantically only because the gates were written to target them. A sixth, unanticipated corruption would still be hash-only.
M08 remains NOT RUN; the undocumented extraction requirement is untouched.
C3 remains C3_CANONICAL_WRITE_FIXED. C3a, C3b and C3c stay red by design.
uncertainty: These gates were verified against the specific corruptions they were built to catch. That is the circularity risk a reader should weigh: a gate written to catch a known mutation will catch it. Their value against UNANTICIPATED corruptions is unmeasured, and the honest way to measure it would be a fresh mutation battery designed by someone who has not seen these gates.
independentlyReproduced: Not yet. Each gate was verified once here.
